key_insight: Explainable machine learning can diagnose Alzheimer’s disease accurately using only routine, low-cost clinical data, potentially supporting faster triage when specialist access is limited.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help clinicians screen cognitive impairment more efficiently with readily available demographic, history, and neuropsychological test data.
method: Trained an explainable deep neural network and a LightGBM classifier.
Used routine clinical variables that can be automatically acquired.
Compared model performance on a large National Alzheimer’s Coordinating Center dataset.
evidence_signal: On 167,364 observations with 1,024 features, the deep neural network reached 90% accuracy and 0.96 ROC-AUC, while LightGBM reached 90% accuracy and 0.97 ROC-AUC.
watch_item: Performance was evaluated under constrained information, so real-world deployment should confirm robustness across sites, populations, and data quality differences.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer's Diagnosis Using Routine and Low-Cost Clinical Data
